biological.citation: Mutations in ACTL6B Cause Neurodevelopmental Deficits and Epilepsy and Lead to Loss of Dendrites in Human Neurons (PMID: 31031012)
biological.summary: ACTL6B knockout in human-derived neurons resulted in profound deficits in dendrite development, which was recapitulated in neurons from individuals with bi-allelic mutations and reversed by genetic repair or exogenous ACTL6B expression. Whole-transcriptome analysis revealed altered BAF complex binding and transcriptional changes in cytoskeletal genes (TPPP, FSCN1) in mutant neural progenitor cells and neurons.
biological.sample_size: 10 bi-allelic mutation carriers, 10 de novo heterozygous mutation carriers

biological.citation: Loss of the neural-specific BAF subunit ACTL6B relieves repression of early response genes and causes recessive autism (PMID: 32312822)
biological.summary: ACTL6B loss-of-function mutations in neurons relieved repression of early response genes including AP1 transcription factors (Fos, Fosl2, Fosb, Junb), increased chromatin accessibility at AP1 binding sites, and altered late response gene expression. Patient mutations destabilized ACTL6B protein in neurons.
biological.sample_size: 6 families with segregating mutations; identified as most significantly mutated gene in Simons Recessive Autism Cohort

biological.citation: An epilepsy-associated ACTL6B variant captures neuronal hyperexcitability in a human induced pluripotent stem cell model (PMID: 33141462)
biological.summary: Patient-derived iPSC neurons with ACTL6B p.(Val421_Cys425del) showed impaired ACTL6B accumulation due to reduced protein stability, dysregulated nBAF target gene expression, and elevated electrophysiological activity consistent with epilepsy phenotype.

biological.citation: MicroRNA-mediated switching of chromatin-remodelling complexes in neural development (PMID: 19561591)
biological.summary: ACTL6B (BAF53b) is a neuron-specific subunit of the nBAF chromatin remodeling complex that replaces BAF53a (ACTL6a) during mitotic exit. This switch is mediated by miR-9* and miR-124 repression of BAF53a, and ACTL6B is essential for post-mitotic neural development and dendritic morphogenesis.

biological.citation: Actl6b knockout mice on two genetic backgrounds exhibited ASD-related behaviors, including social and memory impairments, repetitive behaviors, and hyperactivity (PMID: 32312822)
biological.summary: In Drosophila olfactory system, patient mutations in ACTL6B destabilized the protein and rerouted dendrites to the wrong glomerulus. Humans and mice lacking ACTL6B showed corpus callosum hypoplasia, indicating conserved role in neural connectivity.

biological.citation: Predicting bevacizumab efficacy: the emerging role of ACTL6B in colorectal cancer (PMID: 41522748)
biological.summary: ACTL6B emerged as top predictor of bevacizumab response in colorectal cancer. High ACTL6B transcript predicted better objective response rate (67% vs 31%) and longer overall survival. Mechanistically, ACTL6B transcriptionally repressed S1PR3 and activated PPP2R2B, dampening pro-migratory sphingosine-1-phosphate signaling.

biological.citation: Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy 76: Case Report and Review of Literature (PMID: 36553410)
biological.summary: Comprehensive review of 18 children with DEE76 caused by ACTL6B bi-allelic variants (12 homozygous, 6 compound heterozygous). DEE76 presents as early-onset drug-refractory epilepsy with global developmental delay, hypertonia, microcephaly, and brain delayed myelination.

biological.citation: ASHG 2017 - De novo missense mutation clustering identifies candidate neurodevelopmental disorder genes (S.H. Lelieveld et al.)
biological.summary: ACTL6B identified as candidate NDD gene through spatial clustering analysis of de novo missense mutations in 4,061 mutations from developmental disorder cohorts. Clustering pattern suggests non-haploinsufficiency mechanism (gain-of-function or dominant-negative) rather than loss-of-function.
biological.sample_size: 4,061 de novo missense mutations from published exome studies
biological.significance: p=1.65e-04 for enrichment of known NDD genes among 15 identified

biological.citation: ASHG 2019 - Retrospective whole exome sequencing analysis reveals variants in BAF complex genes associated with global developmental delay, epilepsy, and dysmorphism (J. Lattier et al.)
biological.summary: Retrospective WES analysis of >5,000 variants across BAF complex members identified de novo pathogenic variants in ACTL6B across multiple families with phenotype correlation including speech delay, intellectual disability, seizures, motor delay, and facial dysmorphism.
biological.sample_size: >5,000 variants analyzed; multiple families with ACTL6B variants

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Effectively modeling rare neurodevelopmental disorders: A pilot project identifying a novel chromatin remodelling disease (S.C. Bell et al.)
biological.summary: Family with novel ACTL6B mutation causing severe seizures and developmental delay. Patient-derived iPSC-derived cortical neural progenitor cells showed significantly reduced ACTL6B expression correlated with dysregulation of neuronal differentiation.
